A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HVR-Met. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices support reliable matching despite rewriting and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on 100 extreme-weather events, index-calculation and plotting tasks, and component ablations, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and additionally reports numerical agreement between human and automated evaluations.

M1.justification: The seven-agent architecture, knowledge-supported HVR loop and appendix system prompts are retained. Sections 3.1-3.3 revise the explanation and clarify agent responsibilities; the newly specified five-factor target and 50-turn limit do not establish a change to the implemented method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same five weather categories through 100 diagnostic events, 150 queries covering 30 indices, and 100 plotting tasks covering 20 figure types. Live forecasting systems mentioned in v2's limitations are not newly evaluated scenarios.

E2.justification: The evaluated models remain GPT-5, Gemini-3-Pro-Preview-Thinking, DeepSeek-R1-0528 and Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct. Corresponding ablation configurations are also unchanged; newly cited agent systems are not added comparators.

E3.justification: The reported human-validation sample increases from 20 events (20%) to 30 events (30%). v2 also corrects the written numerical acceptance criteria to use absolute errors. These are reported protocol revisions; unchanged benchmark scores do not establish that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Both ablation suites and the difficulty-stratified analyses remain. Sections 5.2-5.3 add execution-log analysis describing abandonment of specialized tools after one or two repair attempts and plotting failures caused by layer-order occlusion. The existing human-validation analysis is also expanded and quantified.

E5.justification: v1 asserts high human-LLM score correlation without statistics. v2 specifies Pearson correlation and reports coefficients and p-values for five dimensions plus an average in Appendix Table 5. The observation and aggregation basis for these p-values is not explained clearly; neither version reports repeated-run variability.

E6.justification: Scores in Tables 1-4 and Figure 4 are unchanged. v2 adds human-automated correlations ranging from 0.81 to 0.98, averaging 0.88, and observations such as GPT-5 and Gemini completing HVR iterations within three rounds. Removed v1 Table 5 accuracy entries remain available in Figure 4.

T1.justification: v2 corrects the mathematical acceptance rules from signed relative error to absolute relative error and from Reply < 0.05 to |Reply| < 0.05 when GT = 0. Figure 3 is corrected accordingly, resolving disagreement with v1's already absolute-error wording. No new theoretical results or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The system, HVR-loop and benchmark contributions and headline pass rates remain unchanged. However, v2's conclusion newly claims diagnostic proficiency equivalent to a junior forecaster; v1 only claimed useful assistance to human forecasters.

C2.justification: New Section 6 materially qualifies operational applicability: evaluation uses reanalysis, whereas biased live forecasts could cause cascading omissions or misdiagnoses, requiring expert interpretation and local observations. Sections 5.2-5.3 also expand explanations involving meteorological knowledge, tool adherence and visual occlusion. v1 lacked this substantive operational-data limitation.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents the five-factor diagnostic target, 50-turn cap and 20-year climatological reference. It also states that evaluation events postdate model knowledge cutoffs and clarifies plotting-task matching and difficulty criteria. These disclosures improve specificity without demonstrating changed datasets or implementation; appendix prompts remain substantively unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds meteorological diagnosis and forecasting references, a WeatherBench2 citation, and additional scientific-agent references including Guo, Liu and Pantiukhin. These mainly support existing statements; positioning relative to Zephyrus, ClimateAgent and EWE remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Substantial portions of the knowledge-base construction, HVR explanation, benchmark description, results discussion and conclusion are rewritten. Section 4 gains separate workflow and subtask subsections; Limitations and Acknowledgements are added and the Impact Statement is removed. Terminology, the title spelling and author information are also edited.

P2.justification: Figure 1's arrows and Figure 3's error formula are redrawn, Figures 2-3 are relocated, and running headers are added. A new correlation table replaces the redundant appendix accuracy table, whose values remain plotted. Most figure designs and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Clearer HVR specifications, corrected error formulas, quantified human-validation reporting and the explicit reanalysis-versus-live-forecast limitation modestly improve transparency and reproducibility. Core benchmark evidence remains unchanged. Gains are tempered by the unsupported junior-forecaster equivalence claim and Table 5 p-values whose observation and aggregation basis is not reconciled with the stated 30-event sample.
